subject: Scaling of computational costs for spatiotemporal models

messages.author: ed0b2a4a7f094dc3
messages.subject: Scaling of computational costs for spatiotemporal models
parts:
Hello INLA people

In spde spatiotemporal models where the group option is used to build an AR1 temporal process, how does the computation time scales with the number of groups (using the same mesh)? Is it quadratic, cubic, something else? My understanding of what goes on behind the scene is far from sufficient to figure this out.

For a bit of context, I'm trying to build an spde model for zero-inflated negative binomial counts with a weekly AR1 component. Basically, my initial plan was to let the spatial field change weekly according to an AR1 process through the group option. I'm able to run such a model for a given year (with seasonal data e.g. 20 weeks) in a decent amount of time (~1h) using a somewhat coarse mesh (mesh$n = 700). However, increasing the numbers of weeks greatly increases the amount of time it takes to run the model. My complete dataset has 6 years (thus, about 6 * 20 = 120 weeks) and it has been running for 3 days and it is not showing any sign of getting close to a solution. Several elements could potentially explain this (too vague priors, very sparse data in some weeks/years, model too complex for data, unidentifiability...), but I'm also curious about the costs of estimation and how it scales with the number of groups. I may have to use a coarser temporal resolution, change the way I treat the temporal aspect or drop weeks, years with few data.

Thank you!
Francois Rousseu

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Scaling of computational costs for spatiotemporal models
parts:
it should scale about linearly with number of time points, but if you
run into memory issues, then this is another story.

to do this, make sure to run on a linux server (or Mac), and use the
most recent testing version and R-4.1, add

inla.setOption(inla.mode="experimental")

and make sure you use the PARDISO library; see

inla.pardiso()

if that does not work, send me data/code so I can rerun it here

Best
H

messages.author: ed0b2a4a7f094dc3
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Scaling of computational costs for spatiotemporal models
parts:
Thank you for your quick response. This is reassuring that the number of groups should not be an issue. I was already running the model on a Linux server with the latest version of R and INLA. I'm usually using about 75% or less of the available memory so this is probably not my issue. I will make sure to try the experimental mode. I haven't tried the PARDISO library as my current situation does not seem to allow me to use a free license. I will make some further tests with specific years and get back to you off-list if the situation does not seem to improve. I suspect the difficulties are related to data sparseness for some weeks/years.

François Rousseu
